lesson.grammar_point: prepositions of place and giving directions

listenings.text: Oxford Street? Yes, of course, you are very close. Right, so, come out of here and go straight, past the coffee shop, for two blocks. Then you get to a big corner with a bank on it, a big grey one, you cannot miss it, and there you turn left. After that it is two more blocks and you will see a park on your right side. The hotel is just after the park, on Oxford Street, next to a pharmacy with a green sign. It is about eight minutes walking, maybe twelve if you are with children or with bags. If you get to the river, you have gone too far and you need to come back. But honestly, you cannot miss it.

Hello, this is a message about your tour tomorrow morning. The meeting point is not the hotel, so please read this carefully. We meet in the square, next to the big fountain, at nine o'clock. From your hotel it is very simple: turn right when you come out, walk straight for three blocks, and the square is in front of you. It takes about ten minutes with children. Please do not go to the station, because many people go there by mistake and then they miss the bus. If you are late, do not worry: call us and we tell you where we are. And bring something warm, because in the morning the square is cold, even in summer. See you tomorrow at nine.

extra_audio.text: Excuse me. Where is Oxford Street, please? Is it far? Can I walk? So, straight and then left at the corner. Is that right? Thank you very much.

reading.rtitle: How to Find Us -- e-mail from the hotel
paras: Dear Mrs Shimada, thank you for your reservation. Here are simple directions from the station to the hotel. Please print this or save it on your phone, because in the street the signal is not always good.
Come out of the station on the main side, not the side of the buses. Go straight for two blocks, past a coffee shop on your left.
At the second corner there is a big grey bank. Turn left there. Walk two more blocks. You see a small park on your right side.

The hotel is just after the park, on Oxford Street, next to a pharmacy with a green sign. It takes about eight minutes on foot, or twelve minutes with children and bags. If you arrive at the river, you have gone too far: come back two blocks. A taxi from the station takes five minutes and costs about nine pounds.
